subject.title: fix(skills): refuse owner-qualified ClawHub force install over a different owner

question: Should OpenClaw treat owner-qualified `skills install --force` over a differently-owned tracked skill as a hard refusal, even though this tightens the existing `--force` behavior?
rationale: The code fix is narrow and supported, but the new failure mode is an intentional compatibility-sensitive CLI contract change for users who may have used `--force` as a replacement workflow.

options.title: Accept the hard owner-mismatch refusal
options.body: Merge this behavior as the safer owner-scoped contract and require users to uninstall, rename, or use an explicit future transfer path when changing publishers.

options.title: Preserve broader `--force` compatibility
options.body: Ask for a revised patch that keeps forced owner replacement possible, likely with a warning or explicit transfer workflow, at the cost of preserving the clobber path.

options.title: Pause for owner-scoped lifecycle direction
options.body: Hold this PR until the broader ClawHub owner-scoped skill-ref work has a maintainer-approved contract for install, update, verify, and publisher transfer behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept the hard owner-mismatch refusal
recommendation.body: Merge this behavior as the safer owner-scoped contract and require users to uninstall, rename, or use an explicit future transfer path when changing publishers.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and merged the owner-qualified ClawHub lifecycle behavior this PR tightens.
